ex-opacity.text: Make the green quad more opaque: an alpha of 0.8 instead of 0.5. How much of the red quad is still visible through it?

hint.opengl: Only the alpha of the colour the green quad is drawn with changes: the fourth component of its `setVec4("color", …)`.
hint.vulkan: Only the alpha of the green quad's colour in the push constants changes: the fourth component of `constants.color`.
hint.d3d12: Only the alpha of the green quad's colour in the root constants changes: the fourth component of `objectConstants.color`.

ex-sorted.text: Fix the picture the classic way: draw the transparent quads sorted back to front. The blue quad's corner should then show through the green quad.
ex-sorted.hint: The blue quad is the farthest (z = 0) and the green one the nearest (z = 2): swap the two draws so the blue quad is drawn first. Blending and depth writes stay as they are.

ex-depth-mask.text: Keep the wrong order, but turn off depth writes for the transparent quads. What happens where green and blue overlap now – does it look right?

hint.opengl: `glDepthMask(GL_FALSE)` right after the blend function is set, before the transparent quads (the frame starts with `glDepthMask(GL_TRUE)` again). The depth test stays on, so the red quad still hides the blue one.
hint.vulkan: Depth writes are part of the transparent pipeline: its `createPipeline(…)` call takes `depthWriteEnable` after `depthTestEnable`. Keep the depth test on, so the red quad still hides the blue one.
hint.d3d12: Depth writes are part of the transparent pipeline state: `psoDesc.DepthStencilState.DepthWriteMask = D3D12_DEPTH_WRITE_MASK_ZERO` before it is created. The depth test stays on, so the red quad still hides the blue one.
